name: Atlas Labs Automates 70% of Its Finance Workload
excerpt: Atlas Labs connected every system to Euphoria and let AI agents handle categorisation, approvals and reporting.
quote: Their 70% work was automated. Our team now spends its time on analysis instead of data entry.
longQuote: Seventy percent of our finance work is now automated. The agents handle categorisation and approvals, so our team spends its time on analysis and forecasting instead of data entry.
body:
Atlas Labs Had Every Finance Tool It Could Need. What It Still Lacked Was a Finance Function That Could Run Day to Day Without Constant Human Input.

Categorisation, approvals and reporting were all handled by people copying data between systems. The finance team was large, expensive and still late every month, and each new hire added more handoffs rather than more insight. For a 400-person enterprise SaaS company, the operating model simply could not scale any further.

Connect Every System Before Automating

The rollout began by connecting banks, payroll, billing and the CRM to Euphoria in the first week. Every transaction now arrives already enriched with customer, vendor and contract context, which gave the AI agents the complete picture they needed before taking on any work.
bodyContinued:
Let the Agents Do the Routine

Euphoria's AI agents now categorise each transaction and propose the matching invoice or receipt, learning from every correction the finance team makes along the way.

Approvals route automatically based on amount, department and vendor, and the co-pilot drafts a short summary so approvers can decide in seconds. Monthly reports assemble themselves from the reconciled ledger, removing the spreadsheet stage that used to consume the first week of every new month.

The team set confidence thresholds for each type of task. Below them, agents hold the work and ask; above them, they act and log the decision, so automation expanded gradually and safely as the team’s trust in the agents grew.

Keeping Humans in Charge of the Exceptions

Instead of checking every entry, the finance team now reviews a single daily exception queue. Anything the agents are unsure about is escalated with a suggested answer and the reasoning behind it, so most items are resolved with one click.

Every correction feeds back into the agents, which means the exception queue has shrunk steadily since launch. Controllers retain full control and a complete audit trail, while the repetitive volume no longer reaches them.

Seventy Percent Automated, Four Times the Speed

Today 70% of Atlas Labs' finance workload runs end to end without manual input, and reporting is delivered four times faster than before the rollout. Accuracy improved at the same time.

The team itself has changed shape. Analysts who once spent their days on data entry now focus on forecasting, pricing and unit economics, and leadership receives answers to commercial questions in hours instead of weeks. Growth no longer requires more finance headcount. As the integration director says, the team now spends its time on analysis instead of keying in data, which has transformed the function.

name: Radius Passes Its First Audit with Zero Findings
excerpt: Radius built continuous controls into its daily workflow and walked through its first external audit without a single adjustment.
quote: Every number traced back to its source. The auditors asked fewer questions than ever before.
longQuote: Every number traced back to its source. We walked into our first audit with nothing to reconstruct, and the auditors asked fewer questions than any team they had worked with.
body:
Investors and Auditors Move Faster When the Books Are Clean. Radius Walked into Its First External Audit with Nothing to Reconstruct and Nothing to Hide.

Ahead of a growth round, the healthcare platform had never been audited. The finance team expected weeks of gathering evidence, rebuilding schedules and answering questions about historical entries, all while diligence ran in parallel. Rather than prepare for the audit as a one-off project, Radius decided to build controls into its daily work.

Approvals That Leave a Trail Automatically

Every spend approval now happens inside Euphoria's workflow, creating a record of who agreed to what, when and under which policy. Auditors can trace any expense back to the original decision in a few clicks, without anyone digging through email threads or chat history for proof.
bodyContinued:
Logs That Answer Questions

Every change to a transaction, exchange rate or account mapping is logged with the user and timestamp, so the history of any number is visible to anyone who needs it.

Role-based access shows exactly who can post, approve and export, and segregation of duties is enforced by the platform rather than by memory. When the auditors asked for an access review, the team exported it in minutes instead of compiling it by hand across systems.

Period locks prevent silent edits to closed months. Any correction after a close is posted as a visible adjustment in the current period, which gave the auditors confidence that historical figures had not drifted.

Reports That Match the Ledger Every Single Time

Board reports are generated from the same reconciled data the auditors test, so there is no gap between what management presents and what sits in the ledger. Supporting schedules export directly from the system in the format requested.

Continuous controls replaced the usual pre-audit scramble. Exceptions are flagged as they happen and resolved the same week, which meant the team entered fieldwork with a clean ledger instead of a long list of open items.

Zero Findings and a Faster Path Through Diligence

Radius closed its first external audit with zero findings and no adjustments, an outcome the finance director had not expected for a first-time engagement. The auditors asked fewer questions than ever.

The same evidence trail that satisfied the auditors also sped up the growth round. Investors received data-room schedules straight from the system, and diligence finished three weeks faster than planned. The controls now run quietly in the background, so the next audit will feel like an ordinary month. As the finance director puts it, every number traced back to its source and nobody had to reconstruct anything.

name: Goodwell Closes the Books in 48 Hours
excerpt: Goodwell automated matching for its high-volume marketplace transactions and cut close time by eighty percent.
quote: Month end used to take two weeks. Now it is done before the second working day.
longQuote: Month end used to take two weeks of manual matching. Now twelve thousand transactions reconcile themselves, and the books are closed before the second working day of the month.
body:
High-Volume Marketplaces Drown in Small Transactions. Goodwell Needed Reconciliation to Happen Without People, and a Close That No Longer Took Two Weeks.

Twelve thousand payouts, fees and refunds arrived every month, and two full-time controllers spent most of the close matching them by hand. The process took two weeks, left little time for analysis, and grew heavier with every new seller. Yet most of those transactions followed the same handful of predictable patterns.

Find the Patterns Before Automating Them

Before switching anything on, the team analysed a full quarter of transactions inside Euphoria. Five rules described more than ninety percent of the volume, from recurring vendor bills to processor payouts. Those rules became the foundation of the new rules-based reconciliation engine.
bodyContinued:
Automate the Obvious First

Recurring vendors are now matched by reference, amount range and cadence, so the bills that arrive every month reconcile themselves before anyone opens the ledger.

Processor payouts were the next target. Euphoria splits each payout into gross revenue, platform fees and refunds automatically, posting every component to the right account. What once required a controller to rebuild each settlement line by line now happens the moment the bank feed lands.

Customer receipts match open invoices by amount, reference and a configurable date window. Partial payments and small rounding gaps are handled by tolerance rules, so they no longer become manual tickets.

Reviewing Only the Exceptions That Truly Matter

Whatever the rules cannot match becomes a short exception list, reviewed once a day rather than all month. Each item arrives with the most likely match suggested, so most exceptions are cleared in seconds instead of minutes of searching.

Every manual decision can be saved as a new rule with a single click. The exception list has shrunk month after month as the engine learns Goodwell's patterns, and the controllers now spend minutes on it, not hours.

A Forty-Eight Hour Close at Twelve Thousand Items

Goodwell's monthly close now finishes within 48 hours, an eighty percent reduction from the two-week process it replaced. More than 12,000 transactions a month are reconciled automatically.

The bigger win is where the controllers spend their time. Instead of matching receipts, both now focus on margin analysis by category and seller, giving leadership insight that simply did not exist before. The close is also calmer and more predictable, because the work no longer piles up at month end. As the controller puts it, month end used to take two weeks, and now it is done before the second working day.

name: Railspeed Forecasts Runway with Daily Accuracy
excerpt: Railspeed moved from a quarterly spreadsheet forecast to a living model refreshed from the ledger every day.
quote: We finally trust the forecast. It updates itself every morning and the board sees the same numbers we do.
longQuote: We finally trust the forecast. It updates itself every morning straight from the ledger, so the board, the CFO and every team lead are always looking at exactly the same numbers.
body:
A Forecast Is Only Useful If It Is Still True Tomorrow. Railspeed's Quarterly Workbook Rarely Was, and the Leadership Team Had Stopped Relying on It.

Runway was recalculated by hand every quarter from a forty-tab spreadsheet. Sales, operations and finance each kept their own version, none of them matched the bank balance, and by the time a new forecast reached the board it was already out of date. For a Series B logistics business, that uncertainty was expensive.

Start from the Ledger, Not a Spreadsheet

Instead of rebuilding the workbook, the team connected its banks and accounting system to Euphoria. Categorised transactions now feed the forecast directly, so the baseline updates every morning as cash moves rather than waiting for someone to paste in actuals at quarter end.
bodyContinued:
Model Drivers, Not Line Items

Driver-based forecasting replaced hundreds of hard-coded revenue rows. Headcount, fleet size and utilisation now drive the model, so one change flows through everywhere.

Three scenarios were built on the same drivers: base, upside and downside. Leadership can see how a delayed contract or a new depot affects runway in seconds, and finance no longer maintains separate copies of the model for every question a board member happens to ask.

Assumptions are locked each month and every edit is versioned with its author. When a number moves, the team can see exactly which driver changed it and why, which has ended the debates about whose forecast is right.

Sharing One Version of the Truth Across Leadership

The whole leadership team now opens the same runway figure every morning. Operations sees how utilisation affects cash, sales sees the impact of pipeline slips, and finance spends its time explaining the numbers rather than defending them.

The board pack is generated straight from the live model instead of being rebuilt in slides each quarter. Directors receive the same figures the CFO sees, and follow-up questions are answered on the call rather than days later.

Eighteen Months of Runway, Visible Every Morning

Over the following two quarters, forecast accuracy reached 94% against actual results, a level the old workbook never came close to. That accuracy has held as the business expanded.

Railspeed now has eighteen months of runway visibility at any moment, not just at quarter end. That clarity changed how the company makes decisions: hiring plans, fleet investments and pricing changes are tested against live scenarios before they are approved. As the CFO describes it, the team finally trusts the forecast, because it updates itself every morning and the board sees exactly the same numbers.

name: Northstar Scales to Five Entities Without Adding Staff
excerpt: Northstar expanded into three countries and kept a two-person finance team thanks to automated consolidation.
quote: Euphoria changed how our team works. Hard tasks feel easy now, and results beat anything we tried before.
longQuote: Euphoria changed how our team works. We expanded into three new countries and five entities, yet consolidation now runs itself and we never had to hire extra finance staff.
body:
Expanding into Three New Countries Usually Means Hiring a Bigger Finance Team. Northstar Set Out to Grow Its Group Footprint While Keeping the Team at Two.

Each new entity brought its own bank accounts, currency and local accountant. Consolidating the group took a full month of spreadsheet work every quarter, intercompany balances rarely agreed, and the board only ever saw numbers that were already six weeks old by the time the pack reached them.

Map the Group Structure Once, Not Monthly

The rollout started by connecting every subsidiary ledger and bank account to Euphoria and defining ownership percentages up front. From there, the platform built the consolidation tree automatically, and any new entity inherits the mapping and rules of its parent from day one.
bodyContinued:
Automate the Manual Steps

Intercompany invoices and management fees are now identified and eliminated automatically, removing the most error-prone step of every quarterly consolidation.

Currency handling followed. Balances convert at closing, average or historical rates depending on the account type, and Euphoria posts the translation differences on its own. What used to be a fragile chain of lookup formulas is now a set of rules the team reviews once and trusts.

Every elimination and FX adjustment is logged with its source, so the external auditors can trace any consolidated figure back to the original subsidiary entry without asking the team for extra schedules.

Giving the Board Live Numbers Instead of Late Ones

Group reports now refresh automatically whenever a subsidiary closes its period. Directors can drill from any consolidated figure straight down to the underlying transaction, which has turned board meetings from reconciling numbers into discussing them.

Local accountants still own their entities, but they submit through the same workspace rather than emailing workbooks. That single change removed most version conflicts and gave the central team one shared timeline for each close.

Five Entities, One Workspace, No New Finance Hires

Northstar now closes five entities from a single workspace with the same two-person finance team, and it made zero new finance hires throughout an expansion that added three new countries and currencies.

Board reporting moved from six weeks late to effectively real time, and the time saved has been redirected into cash planning across currencies. When the next market opens, setting up its entity takes an afternoon rather than a month of rebuilding spreadsheets. As the CFO put it, Euphoria changed how the team works and made the hardest tasks of running a multi-entity group feel routine.

name: How Lugo Cut Customer Support Costs by 62%
excerpt: Lugo replaced four disconnected tools with Euphoria and automated its entire reconciliation flow.
quote: Support no longer waits on finance. Agents see reconciled payments instantly and close takes three days.
longQuote: Support no longer waits on finance. Our agents see reconciled payments instantly, refunds route themselves for approval, and the monthly close takes three days instead of two weeks.
body:
Scaling a Support-Heavy Fintech Takes More Than Extra Headcount. Lugo Needed Its Billing, Refund and Bank Data to Finally Live in One Trusted Place.

Lugo answered the same billing questions hundreds of times a month because invoices, refunds and bank movements sat in four disconnected tools. Every reply needed a finance colleague to reconcile the numbers by hand first, so tickets stalled for days while customers waited and the monthly close kept slipping.

Stop Being the Middleman for Every Invoice

Support agents had no way to see whether a payment had cleared, so every billing ticket bounced to finance and back again. The first step was giving each agent a live, read-only view of reconciled transactions inside Euphoria, so they could confirm a payment without asking.
bodyContinued:
Replace Matching with Rules

Bank feeds and the payment processor were connected in the first week, and every movement now lands in one ledger already enriched with customer and invoice context.

Euphoria's AI reconciliation engine matches payouts, fees and refunds against open invoices automatically. Refunds are categorised and routed for approval inside the same workflow, leaving a complete audit trail instead of a chain of forwarded emails and screenshots.

Anything the engine cannot match with confidence lands in a single exception queue. Finance reviews it once a day with a suggested answer attached, instead of interrupting their work every hour to chase missing data.

Shifting Support from Chasing to Answering

With reconciled numbers visible to everyone, agents now resolve most billing questions in a single message. Escalations to finance dropped sharply, and customers stopped waiting days for a simple confirmation that their refund had gone out.

Finance, in turn, stopped fielding internal tickets and put its full attention on the close. The approval co-pilot handles routine refund sign-offs, so managers only step in when an amount or reason falls outside policy.

From Reactive Firefighting to Strategic Planning

Within a single quarter, support costs fell by 62% and the monthly close shrank to just three days. Both numbers have held steady in every quarter since, even as transaction volume and the customer base kept growing.

The bigger change is how the team spends its time. Hours that once went into copying figures between tools now go into modelling pricing changes on live data and spotting churn risks early. Lugo's leadership reviews the same reconciled numbers as the support desk, which has removed the debates about whose spreadsheet is right and made every planning conversation faster and calmer.
